userStories.title: ACP Activity Emission — Wire Stream Events into Agent Execution
acceptanceCriteria: When parseAcpxJsonLine() processes a JSON-RPC line with method=session/update and sessionUpdate=agent_message_chunk, it returns activity metadata with kind='message_update' and a non-negative deltaBytes

When parseAcpxJsonLine() processes a JSON-RPC line with method=session/update and sessionUpdate=agent_thought_chunk, it returns activity metadata with kind='thinking_update' and a non-negative deltaBytes

When parseAcpxJsonLine() processes a JSON-RPC line with method=session/update and sessionUpdate=usage_update, it returns activity metadata with kind='usage_update' and populated inputTokens/outputTokens/costUsd fields
The returned activity metadata from parseAcpxJsonLine() never contains raw message or thought text content
agent.call_started is emitted before the acpx process is spawned
agent.process_update { status: 'spawned' } is emitted after PID registration completes
agent.message_update and agent.thinking_update events are emitted during stdout line reading, before the process exits
agent.call_ended is emitted exactly once for every agent.call_started event, across success, error, cancel, and parse failure paths
When the spawned process fails to start, agent.call_ended { status: 'error' } is emitted without a prior agent.call_started
Each physical prompt invocation generates a unique callId via crypto.randomUUID(), distinct from the session name

escalations.reason: Reviewer contradiction: AC5 ("agent.call_started is emitted before the acpx process is spawned") and AC9 ("When the spawned process fails to start, agent.call_ended is emitted without a prior agent.call_started") are mutually exclusive. Emitting call_started before spawn means any spawn failure will always have a prior call_started. The current implementation satisfies AC5; satisfying AC9 as written requires violating AC5. These two ACs cannot both be satisfied without redefining one of them.

suggestedCriteria: agent.process_update { status: 'cancelled' } is emitted when cancelActivePrompt() is called mid-flight
agent.process_update { status: 'stderr' } is emitted when acpx writes to stderr, without including the stderr text content
When parseAcpxJsonLine() receives a non-JSON line, it returns undefined for activity metadata without corrupting parse state
Multiple agent_message_chunk lines in sequence each produce separate agent.message_update events with distinct deltaBytes
callId is generated once at prompt start (crypto.randomUUID) and is referenced unchanged by every event emitted for that turn, from agent.call_started through agent.call_ended

userStories.title: Idle Watchdog Subscriber and Configuration Schema
acceptanceCriteria: When agent.message_update is emitted and 'message_update' is in configured activityKinds, the watchdog resets lastActivityAt for that callId
When agent.thinking_update is emitted and 'thinking_update' is in configured activityKinds, the watchdog resets lastActivityAt for that callId
When agent.usage_update is emitted and 'usage_update' is in configured activityKinds, the watchdog resets lastActivityAt for that callId
When agent.process_update is emitted, the watchdog does NOT reset lastActivityAt, regardless of activityKinds config
In 'observe' mode, when a call exceeds idleTimeoutSeconds without activity, the watchdog logs a warning but does NOT invoke the cancellation function
In 'warn-then-cancel' mode, when a call exceeds idleTimeoutSeconds, the watchdog logs a warning; if activity arrives during cancelGraceSeconds, the cancellation is aborted
In 'cancel' mode, when a call exceeds idleTimeoutSeconds, the watchdog immediately invokes the cancellation function without a grace period
When agent.call_ended is emitted, the watchdog deletes all state and timers for that callId
When the same logical agent operation is cancelled by the watchdog maxRetryAttempts times, the watchdog emits a terminal failure and stops retrying
Config validation rejects idleTimeoutSeconds <= 0 when mode is not 'off'

userStories.title: Failure Classification and Retry for Stale Prompts
acceptanceCriteria: When a prompt is cancelled by the idle watchdog, the adapter returns an AdapterFailure with outcome='fail-stale' and category='availability'
fail-stale triggers the same retry/fallback path as other availability failures (e.g., fail-rate-limit) in AgentManager.runWithFallback
fail-stale does NOT trigger tier escalation or quality escalation in the pipeline
Retry for fail-stale stops after maxRetryAttempts attempts; subsequent stale cancellations for the same logical operation return a terminal failure
When fail-stale retries are exhausted, AgentManager falls back to a configured fallback agent if one exists
When a stale cancellation occurs, complete() returns a structured AdapterFailure — the stale failure text is NOT handed to operation parsers as if it were successful model output
fail-timeout behavior (wall-clock timeout) remains unchanged except for clearer logging that distinguishes it from fail-stale
SessionFailureError carries the fail-stale AdapterFailure so that sendTurn()/runAsSession() propagates the structured failure for the caller to interpret
An integration test verifies that a hanging ACP prompt with no stream activity is cancelled by the idle watchdog before the wall-clock timeout, producing a fail-stale AdapterFailure
An integration test verifies that a prompt emitting periodic agent_thought_chunk lines is NOT cancelled by the watchdog, even when total wall-clock duration approaches the wall-clock timeout
An integration test verifies that a prompt emitting only periodic usage_update lines is NOT cancelled by the watchdog
suggestedCriteria: fail-stale retry count is tracked independently from fail-rate-limit and fail-timeout retry counts per logical agent operation
When the same operation is cancelled by watchdog twice, then succeeds on the third attempt, the retry accounting is reset for the next distinct operation
Fallback agent selection for fail-stale uses the same fallback map and maxHopsPerStory as other availability failures
Log output for a fail-stale recovery path includes: storyId, original agent, retry attempt number, and whether fallback was invoked

analysis:
## Impact Areas

### New files to create
- `src/runtime/agent-stream-events.ts` — AgentStreamEvent type union, concrete event interfaces, and AgentStreamEventBus class
- `src/runtime/middleware/agent-idle-watchdog.ts` — idle watchdog subscriber with timer management
- `src/runtime/middleware/agent-stream-logging.ts` — lightweight stream event logger

### Files to modify
- `src/runtime/index.ts` — add `agentStreamEvents` to NaxRuntime, construct in createRuntime(), wire watchdog
- `src/runtime/middleware/index.ts` — export new attachAgentStreamLogging and attachAgentIdleWatchdog
- `src/config/schemas-infra.ts` — add IdleWatchdogConfigSchema within AgentAcpConfigSchema
- `src/config/runtime-types-agent.ts` — add IdleWatchdogConfig interface within AgentAcpConfig
- `src/agents/acp/parser.ts` — modify parseAcpxJsonLine() to return activity metadata alongside parse state updates
- `src/agents/acp/spawn-client.ts` — add optional stream callback to spawn client, emit activity events during line-reading
- `src/agents/acp/adapter-lifecycle.ts` — thread stream callback through createClient and session helpers
- `src/agents/acp/adapter-session-types.ts` — add stream callback types to AcpClient/AcpSession interfaces
- `src/agents/acp/adapter.ts` — wire stream callback from AgentRunOptions/CompleteOptions through to spawn client
- `src/agents/types.ts` — add stream callback to AgentRunOptions, add callId field, add fail-stale classification
- `src/agents/manager.ts` — thread stream callback, register prompt cancellation in watchdog controller registry
- `src/agents/retry/default-strategy.ts` — extend shouldRetry() to handle fail-stale outcome
- `src/context/engine/types.ts` — add 'fail-stale' to AdapterFailure.outcome union
- `src/operations/call.ts` — ensure stale failure text is not parsed as output
- `src/operations/build-hop-callback.ts` — propagate fail-stale through hop callback
- `src/runtime/session-run-hop.ts` — propagate fail-stale through session run hop
- `src/tui/hooks/usePipelineEvents.ts` — add stream event hook
- `src/tui/App.tsx` — subscribe to stream events
- `src/tui/components/AgentPanel.tsx` — render stream activity indicators
- `src/cli/status.ts` — may need stream event status output

### Key existing patterns to follow
- `src/pipeline/event-bus.ts` (PipelineEventBus) — event bus pattern with typed events, unsubscribe returns, error isolation
- `src/runtime/dispatch-events.ts` (DispatchEventBus) — runtime-level bus with Set-based listeners, try/catch per listener
- `src/runtime/middleware/logging.ts` — subscriber attachment pattern: attach*(bus, ...) => () => void
- `src/runtime/middleware/index.ts` — barrel exports for middleware subscribers
- `src/config/schemas-infra.ts` — Zod schema patterns with .default(), .min(), .max(), .int(), discriminated unions
- `src/config/runtime-types-agent.ts` — TypeScript interfaces mirroring Zod schemas
- `src/agents/retry/default-strategy.ts` — RetryStrategy interface with shouldRetry(AdapterFailure, attempt, ctx) => RetryDecision

### Architecture decisions
1. **Separate bus from DispatchEventBus** — stream events are fire-and-forget, metadata-only, O(active prompts) memory. Dispatch events are final results with full prompt/response.
2. **UUID-based callId** — one physical prompt invocation gets one callId, even if the session has multiple turns. sessionName alone is insufficient.
3. **Default metadata-only payloads** — content fields (raw message text, thought text) are excluded by default. Only deltaBytes, token counts, and cost are emitted.
4. **Watchdog as middleware subscriber** — attaches to AgentStreamEventBus, maintains per-call state Map, uses bounded interval timers.
5. **Config-driven behavior** — mode-based watchdog (off/observe/warn-then-cancel/cancel) with one global idle timeout for first release.
6. **fail-stale as availability failure** — classified under category: "availability" so it triggers agent fallback/retry, not quality escalation.

### Risks
- ACP parser changes must not break existing JSON-RPC parsing or legacy NDJSON parsing
- Watchdog timer management must clean up on agent.call_ended to prevent memory leaks
- Retry strategy changes must preserve existing rate-limit and quality-failure behavior
- TUI changes must handle absent stream events gracefully (watchdog disabled or no active prompts)
- agent_thought_chunk content must never leak into logs or watchdog state

### Dependency order (must implement stories in this sequence)
US-001 → US-002 → US-003 → US-004
US-001 → US-005

US-002, US-003, and US-004 form a sequential chain (each builds on the previous). US-005 can be implemented in parallel with US-002/US-003/US-004 once US-001 is done.
